- On ocaml.org, the **doc-backend fetch bounding** fix remains open, submitted by [Cuihtlauac Alvarado](https://github.com/cuihtlauac): it caps `http_get` responses at a configurable size ceiling, prefers a `search_index_digest` from `status.json` over downloading the full odoc index, and switches `Sidebar_cache` to `Hashtbl.replace` to stop duplicate entries accumulating ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3767](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/pull/3767), fixing [ocaml/ocaml.org#3765](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3765))
- An automated **platform-releases scrape** PR from the `scrape_platform_releases.yml` workflow has been open since June and remains unmerged, carrying 852 additions across 19 files ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3693](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/pull/3693))
- The **Metaprogramming page's** PPX documentation link was updated by [Khalid](https://github.com/khalidbelk) to point at the "latest"-tagged version instead of a four-year-old pinned release, merged this week ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3769](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/pull/3769))
- The dead **lthms blog feed** (soap.coffee, no longer resolving in DNS) was disabled rather than removed by [Cuihtlauac Alvarado](https://github.com/cuihtlauac), preserving the 21 already-archived posts while stopping daily scrape failures, tracked in [ocaml/ocaml.org#3753](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3753) ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3763](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/pull/3763))
- Two automated **OCaml Planet scrapes** merged, pulling in new posts from `cwn`, `ocsigen`, `jonludlam`, `anil`, and `tunbury`, while logging recurring scrape failures for `0branch`, `patricoferris`, `mirage`, and several dead YouTube playlist/channel IDs ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3762](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/pull/3762), [ocaml/ocaml.org#3766](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/pull/3766))
group_summaries.cross_repository_work:
- An ocaml.org issue noting that package pages don't surface **optional dependencies** was raised against the **bytesrw** package page by [Simmo Saan](https://github.com/sim642) ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3768](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3768)) in the same week bytesrw 0.4.1 shipped a large bug-fix release on opam-repository, reported in part by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30716](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30716))
- [Mark Elvers](https://github.com/mtelvers) was active on both repositories: adding OCaml 5.5.1 recognition to ocaml-version on opam-repository ([ocaml/opam-repository#30706](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30706)) and proposing a binaryen build-time optimization there ([ocaml/opam-repository#30664](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30664)), while diagnosing the root cause of ocaml.org's doc-page OOM incident and applying an interim Varnish mitigation ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3765](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3765))
- The ocaml.org OOM fix depends on tooling outside this group: a durable fix requires `ocaml-docs-ci`/voodoo to compute and publish a search-index digest via `status.json`, tracked upstream at [ocurrent/ocaml-docs-ci#193](https://github.com/ocurrent/ocaml-docs-ci/issues/193) and cross-referenced with [ocaml/infrastructure#192](https://github.com/ocaml/infrastructure/issues/192)
group_summaries.notable_discussions:
- [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) opened a **compiler support timeline proposal** through 2030 on opam-repository, sequencing lower-bound raises to OCaml 4.13, 4.14, and eventually 5.2 alongside distro end-of-life dates ([ocaml/opam-repository#30671](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30671))
- [Dmitrii Kosarev](https://github.com/Kakadu) proposed **archiving opam-repository packages whose upstream GitHub repos are marked archived**, identifying candidates such as opam-lock, cconv, ocaml-bigstring, and ocaml-sodium ([ocaml/opam-repository#30550](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30550)), with [Raphaël Proust](https://github.com/raphael-proust) suggesting a discuss.ocaml.org notice for batch archivals
- [Raphaël Proust](https://github.com/raphael-proust) proposed an **`opam-packages-option-static-linking`** convention package for expressing static-linking preferences across dependency trees, closing the issue pending further discussion on the compiler side ([ocaml/opam-repository#29975](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/29975))
- Community pushback on **high-frequency release cadences** for the binaryen/libbinaryen and hegel-ocaml packages, raised by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) and [Calascibetta Romain](https://github.com/dinosaure) on opam-repository, highlighted the shared CI resource cost of near-daily republishing ([ocaml/opam-repository#30664](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30664), [ocaml/opam-repository#30697](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30697))
- On ocaml.org, [Cuihtlauac Alvarado](https://github.com/cuihtlauac) documented a root-cause investigation into intermittent Varnish 503 errors, tracing them to web-server replicas being OOM-killed because rendering any documentation page downloaded the entire odoc search index (371 MB for the `awso` package) into memory just to compute a cache-busting digest ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3765](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3765))
group_summaries.emerging_trends:
- Continued **OCaml 5 compatibility sweep** on opam-repository across older C-stub packages that call unprefixed runtime allocation functions (`alloc_custom`, `alloc_tuple`) instead of the required `caml_`-prefixed equivalents ([ocaml/opam-repository#30663](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30663), [ocaml/opam-repository#30661](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30661))
- The **`v`-prefixed version scheme tripwire** (affecting packages depending on re2, core, and similarly-versioned libraries) continues to require repeated manual bound fixes on opam-repository, prompting calls to fix it upstream ([ocaml/opam-repository#30687](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30687), [ocaml/opam-repository#30688](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30688), [ocaml/opam-repository#30225](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30225))
- Robur-coop's **MirageOS unikernel networking stack** (mnet, utcp, mhttp, bstr) saw coordinated releases on opam-repository in the same week, reflecting active development toward a pure-OCaml TCP/IP and HTTP stack ([ocaml/opam-repository#30674](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30674), [ocaml/opam-repository#30675](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30675), [ocaml/opam-repository#30667](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30667), [ocaml/opam-repository#30665](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30665))
- Maintainers across the group are increasingly pushing back on **unsustainable automation**: opam-repository maintainers on rapid-fire package re-releases that consume shared CI capacity ([ocaml/opam-repository#30664](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30664), [ocaml/opam-repository#30697](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30697)), and ocaml.org's incident response on unbounded automated fetches of generated content ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3767](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/pull/3767))
- On ocaml.org, **dead-feed cleanup** in the OCaml Planet aggregator continues as a recurring maintenance pattern, disabling rather than removing feeds so archived posts keep rendering ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3763](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/pull/3763), tracked in [ocaml/ocaml.org#3753](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3753)), and automated scrape workflows continue to make up the majority of ocaml.org PR volume, with the platform-releases scrape ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3693](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/pull/3693)) sitting unmerged for an extended period

group_summaries.brief_summary: opam shipped 2.6.0~rc1, odoc cut .odoc/.odocl size via compression, and a cross-repo odoc/dune doc-linking bug surfaced.
group_summaries.new_features_summary: odoc shrank .odoc/.odocl files via compression; ocaml-lsp added constructor/whole-call completion snippets; opam fixed a tar.gz install regression.
group_summaries.new_features:
- **odoc** compressed `.odoc`/`.odocl` files for a roughly 4-5x size reduction, memoized doc-comment parsing to cut odoc_driver CPU by ~13% and peak RSS by up to 16%, merged word-run comment storage, removed an internal id-wrapping optimisation (~30% disk reduction), and shared shape-reducer caching, all by [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam) ([ocaml/odoc#1486](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1486), [ocaml/odoc#1480](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1480), [ocaml/odoc#1488](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1488), [ocaml/odoc#1479](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1479), [ocaml/odoc#1487](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1487))
- **odoc** now renders items included via `include functor` for OxCaml code, by [Marek Kubica](https://github.com/Leonidas-from-XIV) ([ocaml/odoc#1452](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1452))
- **ocaml-lsp** added constructor-application and whole-call completion snippets with independent argument placeholders, interactive destruct-generated branch bodies, and `.mli` go-to-implementation support, all by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2212](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2212), [ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2199](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2199), [ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2204](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2204), [ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2074](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2074))
- **ocaml-lsp** semantic highlighting now classifies function parameters, labelled/optional argument modifiers, and built-in vs. user-defined types, by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1857](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/1857), [ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1858](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/1858))
- **opam** fixed a 2.6 performance regression that read `.tar.gz` repositories twice per package install, saving roughly 500ms per install, and shipped **opam 2.6.0~rc1**, by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) ([ocaml/opam#7131](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7131))

group_summaries.new_features_summary: oxcaml/oxcaml added DWARF-5 debug output selection, read-mode Bigarray accessors, all-void records, and dropped legacy runtime-4 shims.
group_summaries.new_features:
- `Bigarray` `Genarray`/`Array0`/`Array1`/`Array2` `get`, `unsafe_get`, and `blit` now require only `@ read` access instead of `@ shared`, letting read-only callers avoid a full shared lock ([oxcaml/oxcaml#5768](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/5768))
- DWARF-5 debug output is now selectable via a `-gdwarf-version` flag, landed by [Mark Shinwell](https://github.com/mshinwell) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6923](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6923)), with follow-ups registering the source file as DWARF-5 line-table file 0 on macOS ([oxcaml/oxcaml#7021](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7021)) and using base-address/offset pairs in DWARF-5 location and range lists ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6926](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6926))
- All-`void` records (fields entirely `void`-layout) are now permitted, by [Will Sturgeon](https://github.com/wrsturgeon) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#7070](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7070))
- Non-scanned unboxed layouts (`bits8`/`16`/`32`/`64`, `float32`, `float64`, `untagged_immediate`, `vec128`/`256`/`512`, `void`, `word`) now cross externality inherently rather than requiring a syntactic `mod external_` annotation, by [Ryan Tjoa](https://github.com/rtjoa) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6973](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6973))
- Legacy OCaml-runtime-4 support markers were removed by [Nick Barnes](https://github.com/NickBarnes) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6707](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6707)): `Config.runtime5` and the deprecated `Gc.eventlog_pause`/`Gc.eventlog_resume` are gone, and `Unix.file_descr`'s kind annotation was simplified to plain `immediate`
- Fixed an allocation-pointer bug on stack overflow ([oxcaml/oxcaml#7020](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7020)) and corrected C stack alignment on stack overflow ([oxcaml/oxcaml#7088](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7088)), both by [Nick Barnes](https://github.com/NickBarnes)
- Fixed `[@unboxable]` crashing on local parameters when the enclosing function is not local-returning, by [Nathanaëlle Courant](https://github.com/Ekdohibs) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6592](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6592))
- CFG dead-code elimination no longer deletes atomic loads whose result is discarded, preserving side effects, by [Xavier Clerc](https://github.com/xclerc) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#7101](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7101))
- Switches sharing the same destination with many arguments are now merged, reducing generated code size, by [Basile Clément](https://github.com/bclement-ocp) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6784](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6784))
- No new-feature activity was recorded this week in oxcaml/opam-repository, oxcaml/merlin, oxcaml/js_of_ocaml, or janestreet/opam-repository

group_summaries.new_features_summary: New runtime_events counters and a corrupt-stream fix, safer Weak.get_copy, Set sharing gains, and a Win32 UNC realpath fix landed in ocaml/ocaml.
group_summaries.new_features:
- **Weak.get_copy** no longer copies continuations, since doing so was unsafe ([ocaml/ocaml#14988](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14988)) by [Jeremy Yallop](https://github.com/yallop); [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) followed up with a PR to deprecate `Weak.get_copy` outright ([ocaml/ocaml#15064](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15064)).
- The **expansiveness check** now accounts for effect cases, closing a soundness gap around `match ... with effect ...` ([ocaml/ocaml#14986](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14986)) by [Jeremy Yallop](https://github.com/yallop).
- **Lambda IR** no longer trusts GADT equations introduced by refutable/partial-match arguments, fixing a native-code segfault ([ocaml/ocaml#15035](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15035), closing [ocaml/ocaml#14898](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14898)) by [Florian Angeletti](https://github.com/Octachron).
- **Runtime_events** gained new counters `EV_C_MAJOR_DIRECT_ALLOCATED_WORDS`, `EV_C_MAJOR_SUSPENDED_ALLOCATED_WORDS`, `EV_C_MAJOR_RESUMED_ALLOCATED_WORDS`, plus an `EV_EXPLICIT_GC_RAMP_UP` span for `Gc.ramp_up` ([ocaml/ocaml#15001](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15001)) by [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist).
- **Runtime_events** consumers that fall behind the producer now see lost-event reporting instead of spurious "corrupt stream" failures ([ocaml/ocaml#15016](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15016), closing [ocaml/ocaml#14151](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14151)) by [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist).
- **Set.union**, **Set.inter** and **Set.diff** gained better complexity on physically-shared sets, avoiding unnecessary traversal/allocation ([ocaml/ocaml#15009](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15009)) by [Nicolás Ojeda Bär](https://github.com/nojb).
- **Unix.realpath** now normalizes Win32 UNC paths correctly ([ocaml/ocaml#15056](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15056), closing [ocaml/ocaml#15044](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15044)) by [Nicolás Ojeda Bär](https://github.com/nojb).
- Parser precedence for the **`with module type`** constraint was fixed ([ocaml/ocaml#14978](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14978)) by [314eter](https://github.com/314eter).
- The **power backend** now emits `fsqrt` directly instead of calling into C, matching the earlier riscv change ([ocaml/ocaml#15006](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15006)) by [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham).
- **libunix** build fixes for Cygwin/mingw covering `gethostname`/IPv6 guards, blocking-section handling around `realpath`/`lockf`, and root registration ([ocaml/ocaml#14740](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14740), [ocaml/ocaml#14921](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14921)) by [Antonin Décimo](https://github.com/MisterDA).
- No new features were recorded in [ocaml/RFCs](https://github.com/ocaml/RFCs) this week.
group_summaries.group_overview:

- [ocaml/RFCs](https://github.com/ocaml/RFCs) recorded no commits, issues, or PRs in this window.

group_summaries.activity_summary: ocaml/ocaml had 11 new PRs opened spanning codegen, tooling, and governance, plus ongoing link-time-linking and GC-pacing work; ocaml/RFCs was quiet.
group_summaries.activity:
- Eleven PRs were opened and remain open in ocaml/ocaml, covering codegen (dead-code elimination of discarded atomic loads, [ocaml/ocaml#15045](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15045) by [Xavier Clerc](https://github.com/xclerc)), tooling (`ocamllex` cleanup on a fatal missing-case warning, [ocaml/ocaml#15048](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15048) by [cui fliter](https://github.com/cuishuang); a new `EV_PROCESS_CREATE` lifecycle event and CI curl-retry/opam-validation hardening, [ocaml/ocaml#15049](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15049) and [ocaml/ocaml#15050](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15050) by [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist)), typing (an escaped-`Equality_trace` fix, [ocaml/ocaml#15052](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15052) by [Samuel Vivien](https://github.com/samsa1); a `[@@deprecated_unlabelled]` attribute proposal, [ocaml/ocaml#15054](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15054) by [Nicolás Ojeda Bär](https://github.com/nojb)), scheduling (always advancing the work counter in idle slices, [ocaml/ocaml#15062](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15062) by [Nick Barnes](https://github.com/NickBarnes)), governance ([ocaml/ocaml#15063](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15063), [ocaml/ocaml#15064](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15064)), CI (disabling the beyond-2038 check on 32-bit CI, [ocaml/ocaml#15065](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15065) by [Olivier Nicole](https://github.com/OlivierNicole)), and testing (skipping the AFL fuzz test without `--with-afl`, [ocaml/ocaml#15066](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15066) by [@akashchamp](https://github.com/akashchamp), addressing [ocaml/ocaml#15046](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15046)).
- [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27) opened parsetree support for wildcards/holes in expressions and module expressions ([ocaml/ocaml#15051](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15051)), which merged just after this reporting window closed.
- Runtime_events work continued from [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist) beyond the merged counters and corrupt-stream fix, with open documentation improvements ([ocaml/ocaml#15039](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15039)) and lost-word truncation handling ([ocaml/ocaml#15010](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15010)).
- Three OSEC security-advisory reference PRs were merged by [Hannes Mehnert](https://github.com/hannesm) ([ocaml/ocaml#15059](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15059), [ocaml/ocaml#15060](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15060), [ocaml/ocaml#15061](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15061)).
- Backend/codegen work continued with an open PR to drop redundant memory-model fences around atomic RMWs on AArch64 ([ocaml/ocaml#14936](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14936) by [Sebastian Pop](https://github.com/sebpop)) and a proposal to emit `clz`/`ctz` primitives on amd64/arm64 ([ocaml/ocaml#15018](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15018) by [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham)).
- Larger in-flight proposals remain open: [Raphaël Proust](https://github.com/raphael-proust)'s link-time-linking design ([ocaml/ocaml#14895](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14895)), [Damien Doligez](https://github.com/damiendoligez)'s new GC-pacing logic ([ocaml/ocaml#14796](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14796)), [Vincent Laviron](https://github.com/lthls)'s support for unlimited non-constant constructors ([ocaml/ocaml#14507](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14507)), [Florian Angeletti](https://github.com/Octachron)'s structured compiler diagnostics ([ocaml/ocaml#13766](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/13766)), and [Jeannalyse](https://github.com/Jeannalyse)'s new `Hashtbl` implementation ([ocaml/ocaml#14956](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14956)) and `Atomic.compare_and_exchange` addition ([ocaml/ocaml#14912](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14912)).
- Two long-dormant PRs were closed: an RFC to add a single file to the load path ([ocaml/ocaml#9056](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/9056) by [Nicolás Ojeda Bär](https://github.com/nojb)) and `Lambda.shallow_fold_left` ([ocaml/ocaml#8784](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/8784) by [Vladimir Keleshev](https://github.com/keleshev)).
- No activity was recorded in [ocaml/RFCs](https://github.com/ocaml/RFCs) this week.

- **GADT/type-soundness edge cases** keep surfacing, from the Lambda-IR value-kind segfault fix ([ocaml/ocaml#15035](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15035), closing [ocaml/ocaml#14898](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14898)) to open reports on module-type subtyping with present/absent aliases ([ocaml/ocaml#13976](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/13976)).

- **Project governance** saw concrete action, with a new maintainer added and inactive ones proposed for retirement in the same cycle ([ocaml/ocaml#15057](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15057), [ocaml/ocaml#15063](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15063)), while ocaml/RFCs itself stayed inactive despite ocaml/ocaml's documentation now pointing larger proposals there ([ocaml/ocaml#15055](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15055)).

group_summaries.new_features_summary: eio added Process.environment/getenv_opt, a new Eio_unix.File module, and Windows rename plus NT path/stat fixes.
group_summaries.new_features:
- [ocaml-multicore/eio](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio): Added `Eio.Process.environment` and `Eio.Process.getenv_opt` for reading process environment variables, with `Env.get_opt` changed to return `None` rather than raising `Invalid_argument` for invalid names, by [Patrick Ferris](https://github.com/patricoferris) with review from [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) and [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([ocaml-multicore/eio#923](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/923))
- New `Eio_unix.File` module adding `import_rw` and `import_ro` to wrap arbitrary Unix file descriptors as Eio files, closing a gap where `Eio_unix.Net.import_socket_stream` was the only option and didn't support operations like `pread`, by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([ocaml-multicore/eio#937](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/937))
- Windows backend gained `rename` support, handling Win32's differing overwrite semantics for files versus directories (FAT volumes cannot replace a directory), by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([ocaml-multicore/eio#934](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/934))
- Windows NT path handling and `stat`/symlink fixes: corrected an uninitialized-handle check in the `openat`/`unlinkat` stubs that misreported failures, fixed `nofollow` dropping directory/non-directory constraints so `stat` kinds worked again, fixed ELOOP symlink recovery resolving against the process directory instead of the sandbox root, fixed unmapped `Unix` errors escaping `open_in`, stopped `stat` from creating a missing file, and made `stat ~follow:false` actually avoid following the link, resolving [ocaml-multicore/eio#931](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/931), by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([ocaml-multicore/eio#932](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/932))
- Fixed a gcc `calloc-transposed-args` warning in `fork_action.c` by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([ocaml-multicore/eio#933](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/933))

group_summaries.activity:
- [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) opened **Windows process spawning support** ([ocaml-multicore/eio#936](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/936)), layered on the still-open pipes fix ([ocaml-multicore/eio#929](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/929)); [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) gave detailed review feedback on the child-wait/cancellation logic, suggesting a simplified `Fiber.fork_daemon` pattern modeled on `eio_posix`'s existing approach
- **Anonymous pipes on Windows** ([ocaml-multicore/eio#929](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/929)) remains a draft, with [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) investigating whether cancellation requires a move to IOCP after finding that `Unix.write` on a full pipe raises `EPIPE` and large writes deadlock
- Issue [ocaml-multicore/eio#935](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/935), an intermittent `eio_linux` spawn failure with `Unix.EUNKNOWNERR 26` (`ETXTBSY`), was closed after [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) and [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) traced it to an upstream `io_uring` kernel bug, reproduced it directly against `liburing`, and got confirmation from the maintainer that a fix is planned for kernel 7.4
- Issue [ocaml-multicore/eio#931](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/931), Windows paths being passed unqualified to `NtCreateFile`, was closed via the fixes in [ocaml-multicore/eio#932](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/932), verified against the `ocaml-forester` test suite in collaboration with [Kento Okura](https://github.com/kentookura)
- Issue [ocaml-multicore/eio#925](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/925), a request for hard-link support (`Eio.Path.link`) using `linkat` to avoid TOCTOU races when extracting untrusted OCI tar archives, remains open, with [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) noting it is queued behind the Windows symlink work
group_summaries.notable_discussions:
- Investigation into [ocaml-multicore/eio#935](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/935) combined `bpftrace` kernel tracing and a minimal C reproduction against `liburing` to show that a file descriptor closed before `execve` was nonetheless still considered open by the kernel on ZFS (but not ext4); [Jens Axboe](https://x.com/axboe) confirmed it as a known `io_uring` kernel bug with a fix planned for 7.4, so no change was needed in eio itself
- Design discussion on [ocaml-multicore/eio#923](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/923) between [Patrick Ferris](https://github.com/patricoferris) and [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) over whether environment access should live on `Eio.Process.mgr` or a separate `Vars` capability, settled by benchmarking `get_all`/`get_opt` versus a direct accessor and by the observation that anyone spawning processes already has environment access
- Review of [ocaml-multicore/eio#936](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/936) surfaced a discussion on correct cancellation semantics for waiting on a Windows child process, with [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) proposing a `Fiber.fork_daemon`-based pattern that signals the process on switch cancellation while still awaiting its exit
group_summaries.emerging_trends:
- Windows backend completeness remained the dominant focus in eio — process spawning ([ocaml-multicore/eio#936](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/936)), anonymous pipes ([ocaml-multicore/eio#929](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/929)), rename ([ocaml-multicore/eio#934](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/934)), and NT path/stat handling ([ocaml-multicore/eio#932](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/932), [ocaml-multicore/eio#931](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/931)) — driven by regression testing against the real-world `ocaml-forester` project with [Kento Okura](https://github.com/kentookura)
- Recurring attention to capability-safety in filesystem APIs, seen both in the Windows symlink/stat fixes in [ocaml-multicore/eio#932](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/932) and in the hard-link request in [ocaml-multicore/eio#925](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/925), which asks for `linkat`-based semantics to avoid TOCTOU races when extracting untrusted archives
- The other eight repositories in the group (domainslib, ocaml-uring, meio, saturn, eio-trace, picos, kcas, ocaml-iomux) had no recorded activity this week

weekly_summary.brief_summary: opam shipped 2.6.0-rc1 as x509 1.2.0 cascaded breaking TLS-stack releases, while oxcaml advanced DWARF-5 debug info and LTO prototyping.
weekly_summary.new_features_summary: opam 2.6.0-rc1 released, x509 1.2.0 cascaded TLS/DNS updates, oxcaml shipped DWARF-5 debug output, and eio gained Windows rename support.
weekly_summary.new_features:
- __RUMINANT:tools__ [ocaml/opam](https://github.com/ocaml/opam) published the [2.6.0-rc1](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/releases/tag/2.6.0-rc1) release candidate after fixing a performance regression that read `.tar.gz` repositories twice per package install, saving roughly 500ms per install ([ocaml/opam#7131](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7131)) by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate); the same candidate was mirrored as 8 packages on opam-repository ([ocaml/opam-repository#30686](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30686)).
- __RUMINANT:ecosystem__ **x509 1.2.0** shipped breaking changes to `Distinguished_name` equality/matching and RFC 9525 hostname validation by [Hannes Mehnert](https://github.com/hannesm) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30712](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30712)), cascading same-day releases of tls 2.1.3 ([ocaml/opam-repository#30725](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30725)), dns 10.2.6 ([ocaml/opam-repository#30726](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30726)), letsencrypt 2.1.1 ([ocaml/opam-repository#30727](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30727)), albatross 2.8.1 ([ocaml/opam-repository#30728](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30728)), and ca-certs-nss 3.129 ([ocaml/opam-repository#30713](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30713)).
- __RUMINANT:oxcaml__ DWARF-5 debug output became selectable via a `-gdwarf-version` flag by [Mark Shinwell](https://github.com/mshinwell) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6923](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6923)), with follow-ups for DWARF-5 line-table file registration ([oxcaml/oxcaml#7021](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7021)) and base-address/offset range lists ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6926](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6926)); all-`void` records are now permitted ([oxcaml/oxcaml#7070](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7070)) by [Will Sturgeon](https://github.com/wrsturgeon), and `Bigarray` accessors now only require `@ read` access instead of `@ shared` ([oxcaml/oxcaml#5768](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/5768)).
- __RUMINANT:core__ **Runtime_events** gained new major-heap allocation counters and a `Gc.ramp_up` span ([ocaml/ocaml#15001](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15001)) plus lost-event reporting to replace spurious "corrupt stream" failures ([ocaml/ocaml#15016](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15016), closing [ocaml/ocaml#14151](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14151)), both by [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist); Lambda IR no longer trusts GADT equations from refutable/partial-match arguments, fixing a native-code segfault ([ocaml/ocaml#15035](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15035)) by [Florian Angeletti](https://github.com/Octachron); **Set.union/inter/diff** gained better complexity on physically-shared sets ([ocaml/ocaml#15009](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15009)) by [Nicolás Ojeda Bär](https://github.com/nojb).
- __RUMINANT:multicore__ [ocaml-multicore/eio](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio) added `Eio.Process.environment`/`getenv_opt` ([ocaml-multicore/eio#923](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/923)), a new `Eio_unix.File` module for wrapping arbitrary Unix file descriptors ([ocaml-multicore/eio#937](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/937)) by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5), and Windows `rename` support handling FAT/NTFS overwrite semantics ([ocaml-multicore/eio#934](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/934)) by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm).
- __RUMINANT:tools__ **odoc** compressed `.odoc`/`.odocl` files for a roughly 4-5x size reduction and memoized doc-comment parsing to cut driver CPU by ~13% ([ocaml/odoc#1486](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1486), [ocaml/odoc#1480](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1480)) by [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam); **ocaml-lsp** added constructor-application and whole-call completion snippets plus `.mli` go-to-implementation ([ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2212](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2212), [ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2074](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2074)) by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg).
- __RUMINANT:ecosystem__ **tyxml 5.0.0** reworked its API to follow the current WHATWG HTML living standard and SVG 2 ([ocaml/opam-repository#30641](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30641)) by [Vincent Balat](https://github.com/balat); new packages included **json-pointer** (RFC 6901/6902/8620 support for `jsont`) by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30656](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30656)), **secret** (zeroized out-of-heap secret memory) and **kube** (typed Kubernetes client) by [Ville Vesilehto](https://github.com/thevilledev) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30672](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30672), [ocaml/opam-repository#30662](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30662)), and Robur-coop's MirageOS networking stack additions **mnet**, **utcp**, **mhttp**, and **bstr** by [Calascibetta Romain](https://github.com/dinosaure) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30674](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30674), [ocaml/opam-repository#30675](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30675)).

weekly_summary.activity:
